task.title: Synthetic offline search scale benchmark
task.original_goal: Create a deterministic synthetic offline search/index benchmark fixture generator for 100, 1,000 and 10,000 fictional articles; create fixtures only in temporary benchmark directories and measure index size/build time. Do not change runtime guides, generated shipping assets, CI or existing production index; avoid dependencies on unmerged cycle 001.
task.scope: Add a standalone stdlib-only Python benchmark under scripts/ which generates completely fictional in-memory content and temporary files to measure build times, compressed index size and representative query latency. Preserve app/runtime formats and never touch shipping assets.
verification_plan: Run script --help and small smoke run with e.g. 100 synthetic documents in GitHub Actions or approved runner
Verify fixed seed gives same generated term/postings counts and deterministic shard file hashes across repeated runs
Verify output JSON contains document count, compressed bytes, build and query timings and clear hardware caveats
Ensure no writes to app/src/main/assets or content/offline_knowledge_articles.json
At larger 1000/10000 sizes test in bounded public CI only where time budget allows

acceptance_criteria: Script generates strictly synthetic fixture documents at 100, 1000, and 10000 counts; no user-visible guides
Deterministic seeded fixture text and index contents, using temporary directory rather than tracked assets
Outputs machine-readable size, build duration and cold query timing per count; labels results as CI-host metrics not P30/device measurements
Standard-library only; bounded runtime and peak memory where possible; no network or third-party packages
Automated smoke/determinism test included and executed in CI with actual logs; no modifications to runtime search logic or published content
excluded_scope: Publishing synthetic fixtures into APK or shipping guides
Assuming Linux CI timings predict P30 device latency
Automatic merging, deployment, user data, CI secrets
